Here \(s=\dfrac{a+b+c}{2}=\dfrac{18+24+30}{2}=36\). Note \(18^2+24^2=324+576=900=30^2\), so the triangle is right angled at \(C\).

(i) By the cosine rule, \(\cos A=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}=\dfrac{576+900-324}{2(24)(30)}=\dfrac{1152}{1440}=\dfrac{4}{5}\).

(ii) \(\sin\dfrac{A}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{bc}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(12)(6)}{(24)(30)}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{72}{720}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\).

(iii) \(\cos\dfrac{A}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{bc}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(36)(18)}{720}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{648}{720}}=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\).

(iv) \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2}=\dfrac{\sin(A/2)}{\cos(A/2)}=\dfrac{1/\sqrt{10}}{3/\sqrt{10}}=\dfrac{1}{3}\).

(v) \(A(\triangle ABC)=\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}=\sqrt{(36)(18)(12)(6)}=\sqrt{46656}=216\) sq. units.

(vi) \(\sin A=2\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{A}{2}=2\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\cdot\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{10}}=\dfrac{6}{10}=\dfrac{3}{5}\).

Let \(r\) be the inradius and \(s=\dfrac{a+b+c}{2}\) the semi-perimeter. Using the standard result \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2}=\dfrac{r}{s-a}\), and noting \(b+c-a=(a+b+c)-2a=2(s-a)\), we get
\((b+c-a)\tan\dfrac{A}{2}=2(s-a)\cdot\dfrac{r}{s-a}=2r\).
Similarly, \(c+a-b=2(s-b)\) gives \((c+a-b)\tan\dfrac{B}{2}=2(s-b)\cdot\dfrac{r}{s-b}=2r\), and \(a+b-c=2(s-c)\) gives \((a+b-c)\tan\dfrac{C}{2}=2(s-c)\cdot\dfrac{r}{s-c}=2r\).
\(\therefore (b+c-a)\tan\dfrac{A}{2}=(c+a-b)\tan\dfrac{B}{2}=(a+b-c)\tan\dfrac{C}{2}=2r\). Hence proved.

Using the half-angle formulas \(\sin\dfrac{A}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{bc}}\), \(\sin\dfrac{B}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(s-c)(s-a)}{ca}}\) and \(\sin\dfrac{C}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(s-a)(s-b)}{ab}}\),
\(\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\sin\dfrac{C}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(s-a)^2(s-b)^2(s-c)^2}{a^2b^2c^2}}=\dfrac{(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}{abc}\).
By Heron's formula \([A(\triangle ABC)]^2=s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)\), so \((s-a)(s-b)(s-c)=\dfrac{[A(\triangle ABC)]^2}{s}\).
\(\therefore \sin\dfrac{A}{2}\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\sin\dfrac{C}{2}=\dfrac{[A(\triangle ABC)]^2}{abc\,s}=\dfrac{[A(\triangle ABC)]^2}{abcs}\). Hence proved.

By the sine rule \(a=2R\sin A,\ b=2R\sin B,\ c=2R\sin C\), so
\(\dfrac{b-c}{a}=\dfrac{\sin B-\sin C}{\sin A}=\dfrac{2\cos\frac{B+C}{2}\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{2\sin\frac{B+C}{2}\cos\frac{B+C}{2}}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{\sin\frac{B+C}{2}}\),
using \(\sin A=\sin(B+C)=2\sin\frac{B+C}{2}\cos\frac{B+C}{2}\).
Since \(\dfrac{B+C}{2}=\dfrac{\pi-A}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{A}{2}\), we have \(\sin\dfrac{B+C}{2}=\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{b-c}{a}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{\cos\frac{A}{2}}\ \Rightarrow\ \sin\left(\dfrac{B-C}{2}\right)=\left(\dfrac{b-c}{a}\right)\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\). Hence proved.

Using \(\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}=\dfrac{1-\cos C}{2}\) and \(\sin^2\dfrac{A}{2}=\dfrac{1-\cos A}{2}\),
\(2\left\{a\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}+c\sin^2\dfrac{A}{2}\right\}=a(1-\cos C)+c(1-\cos A)=(a+c)-(a\cos C+c\cos A)\).
By the projection rule, \(b=a\cos C+c\cos A\).
\(\therefore 2\left\{a\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}+c\sin^2\dfrac{A}{2}\right\}=a+c-b=a-b+c\). Hence proved.

By the sine rule \(a=2R\sin A,\ b=2R\sin B,\ c=2R\sin C\). Then
\(a\sin A-b\sin B=2R(\sin^2 A-\sin^2 B)=2R\,\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B)\),
using \(\sin^2 A-\sin^2 B=\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B)\).
Since \(A+B=\pi-C\), \(\sin(A+B)=\sin C\), so
\(a\sin A-b\sin B=2R\sin C\,\sin(A-B)=c\sin(A-B)\). Hence proved.

By the projection rule, \(c=a\cos B+b\cos A\ \Rightarrow\ c-b\cos A=a\cos B\), and \(b=a\cos C+c\cos A\ \Rightarrow\ b-c\cos A=a\cos C\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{c-b\cos A}{b-c\cos A}=\dfrac{a\cos B}{a\cos C}=\dfrac{\cos B}{\cos C}\). Hence proved.

By the sine rule \(a=2R\sin A,\ b=2R\sin B,\ c=2R\sin C\). Then
\((b^2-c^2)\sin A=4R^2(\sin^2 B-\sin^2 C)\sin A=4R^2\,\sin(B+C)\sin(B-C)\,\sin A\),
using \(\sin^2 B-\sin^2 C=\sin(B+C)\sin(B-C)\).
Since \(B+C=\pi-A\), \(\sin(B+C)=\sin A\), so
\((b^2-c^2)\sin A=4R^2\sin^2 A\,\sin(B-C)=a^2\sin(B-C)\).
\(\therefore a^2\sin(B-C)=(b^2-c^2)\sin A\). Hence proved.

By the cosine rule \(\cos B=\dfrac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2ac}\) and \(\cos A=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}\). Then
\(ac\cos B=\dfrac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2}\) and \(bc\cos A=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2}\).
\(\therefore ac\cos B-bc\cos A=\dfrac{(a^2+c^2-b^2)-(b^2+c^2-a^2)}{2}=\dfrac{2a^2-2b^2}{2}=a^2-b^2\). Hence proved.

By the cosine rule,
\(\dfrac{\cos A}{a}=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2abc},\quad \dfrac{\cos B}{b}=\dfrac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2abc},\quad \dfrac{\cos C}{c}=\dfrac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2abc}\).
Adding these,
\(\dfrac{\cos A}{a}+\dfrac{\cos B}{b}+\dfrac{\cos C}{c}=\dfrac{(b^2+c^2-a^2)+(a^2+c^2-b^2)+(a^2+b^2-c^2)}{2abc}=\dfrac{a^2+b^2+c^2}{2abc}\). Hence proved.

Using \(\cos 2A=1-2\sin^2 A\) and the sine rule \(\dfrac{\sin A}{a}=\dfrac{1}{2R}\) (so \(\dfrac{\sin^2 A}{a^2}=\dfrac{1}{4R^2}\)),
\(\dfrac{\cos 2A}{a^2}=\dfrac{1-2\sin^2 A}{a^2}=\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{2\sin^2 A}{a^2}=\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{1}{2R^2}\).
Similarly, \(\dfrac{\cos 2B}{b^2}=\dfrac{1}{b^2}-\dfrac{1}{2R^2}\). Subtracting,
\(\dfrac{\cos 2A}{a^2}-\dfrac{\cos 2B}{b^2}=\left(\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{1}{2R^2}\right)-\left(\dfrac{1}{b^2}-\dfrac{1}{2R^2}\right)=\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{1}{b^2}\). Hence proved.

\(\tan\dfrac{B}{2}-\tan\dfrac{C}{2}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B}{2}\cos\frac{C}{2}-\cos\frac{B}{2}\sin\frac{C}{2}}{\cos\frac{B}{2}\cos\frac{C}{2}}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{\cos\frac{B}{2}\cos\frac{C}{2}}\), and similarly \(\tan\dfrac{B}{2}+\tan\dfrac{C}{2}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B+C}{2}}{\cos\frac{B}{2}\cos\frac{C}{2}}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{\tan\frac{B}{2}-\tan\frac{C}{2}}{\tan\frac{B}{2}+\tan\frac{C}{2}}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{\sin\frac{B+C}{2}}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{\cos\frac{A}{2}}\), since \(\sin\dfrac{B+C}{2}=\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\).
By the sine rule, \(\dfrac{b-c}{a}=\dfrac{\sin B-\sin C}{\sin A}=\dfrac{2\cos\frac{B+C}{2}\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{2\sin\frac{B+C}{2}\cos\frac{B+C}{2}}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{\sin\frac{B+C}{2}}=\dfrac{\sin\frac{B-C}{2}}{\cos\frac{A}{2}}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{b-c}{a}=\dfrac{\tan\frac{B}{2}-\tan\frac{C}{2}}{\tan\frac{B}{2}+\tan\frac{C}{2}}\). Hence proved.

[Textbook note: As printed, with the HALF-angle cotangents \(\cot\frac{A}{2},\cot\frac{B}{2},\cot\frac{C}{2}\), the result does not hold when \(a^2,b^2,c^2\) are in A.P. (those half-angle cotangents are in A.P. precisely when \(a,b,c\) are in A.P.). The standard, correct result for the hypothesis \(a^2,b^2,c^2\) in A.P. is that \(\cot A,\cot B,\cot C\) are in A.P., proved below.]

By the cosine and sine rules,
\(\cot A=\dfrac{\cos A}{\sin A}=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}\cdot\dfrac{2R}{a}=\dfrac{R(b^2+c^2-a^2)}{abc}\).
Similarly \(\cot B=\dfrac{R(a^2+c^2-b^2)}{abc}\) and \(\cot C=\dfrac{R(a^2+b^2-c^2)}{abc}\).
Given \(a^2,b^2,c^2\) in A.P., we have \(a^2+c^2=2b^2\).
Now \(\cot A+\cot C=\dfrac{R}{abc}\big[(b^2+c^2-a^2)+(a^2+b^2-c^2)\big]=\dfrac{R}{abc}(2b^2)\).
Also \(2\cot B=\dfrac{2R}{abc}(a^2+c^2-b^2)=\dfrac{2R}{abc}(2b^2-b^2)=\dfrac{R}{abc}(2b^2)\).
\(\therefore \cot A+\cot C=2\cot B\), i.e. \(\cot A,\cot B,\cot C\) are in A.P. Hence proved.

Since \(C=90^\circ\), \(A+B=90^\circ\), so \(\cos B=\sin A\) and \(\sin B=\cos A\). Then
\(\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B=\sin^2 A-\cos^2 A\).
In the right triangle (right angle at \(C\)), \(c\) is the hypotenuse, so \(\sin A=\dfrac{a}{c},\ \cos A=\dfrac{b}{c}\), with \(c^2=a^2+b^2\). Hence
\(\sin(A-B)=\dfrac{a^2}{c^2}-\dfrac{b^2}{c^2}=\dfrac{a^2-b^2}{a^2+b^2}\). Hence proved.

By the cosine rule \(\cos A=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}\) and \(\cos B=\dfrac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2ac}\). Then
\(\dfrac{\cos A}{a}=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2abc}\) and \(\dfrac{\cos B}{b}=\dfrac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2abc}\).
Given \(\dfrac{\cos A}{a}=\dfrac{\cos B}{b}\), so \(b^2+c^2-a^2=a^2+c^2-b^2\ \Rightarrow\ 2b^2=2a^2\ \Rightarrow\ a=b\).
\(\therefore\) the triangle is isosceles. Hence proved.

By the sine rule \(\sin A=\dfrac{a}{2R},\ \sin B=\dfrac{b}{2R},\ \sin C=\dfrac{c}{2R}\). The given condition \(\sin^2 A+\sin^2 B=\sin^2 C\) becomes
\(\dfrac{a^2}{4R^2}+\dfrac{b^2}{4R^2}=\dfrac{c^2}{4R^2}\ \Rightarrow\ a^2+b^2=c^2\).
Then \(\cos C=\dfrac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2ab}=0\), so \(C=90^\circ\).
\(\therefore\) the triangle is right angled. Hence proved.

Since \(\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta\), each factor \(\cos^2 B-\cos^2 C=\sin^2 C-\sin^2 B\), and similarly for the others. So the expression becomes
\(a^2(\sin^2 C-\sin^2 B)+b^2(\sin^2 A-\sin^2 C)+c^2(\sin^2 B-\sin^2 A)\).
By the sine rule \(\sin^2 X=\dfrac{x^2}{4R^2}\), so this equals
\(\dfrac{1}{4R^2}\left[a^2(c^2-b^2)+b^2(a^2-c^2)+c^2(b^2-a^2)\right]=\dfrac{1}{4R^2}\big[a^2c^2-a^2b^2+a^2b^2-b^2c^2+b^2c^2-a^2c^2\big]=\dfrac{1}{4R^2}\cdot 0=0\).
Hence proved.

Note that \(c^2-a^2+b^2=b^2+c^2-a^2=2bc\cos A\) (cosine rule). Hence, using the sine rule \(\sin A=\dfrac{a}{2R}\),
\((c^2-a^2+b^2)\tan A=2bc\cos A\tan A=2bc\sin A=2bc\cdot\dfrac{a}{2R}=\dfrac{abc}{R}\).
Similarly \((a^2-b^2+c^2)\tan B=2ac\cos B\tan B=2ac\sin B=\dfrac{abc}{R}\), and \((b^2-c^2+a^2)\tan C=2ab\cos C\tan C=2ab\sin C=\dfrac{abc}{R}\).
\(\therefore (c^2-a^2+b^2)\tan A=(a^2-b^2+c^2)\tan B=(b^2-c^2+a^2)\tan C=\dfrac{abc}{R}\). Hence proved.

Using \(\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}=\dfrac{1+\cos C}{2}\) and \(\cos^2\dfrac{A}{2}=\dfrac{1+\cos A}{2}\),
\(a\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}+c\cos^2\dfrac{A}{2}=\dfrac{a(1+\cos C)+c(1+\cos A)}{2}=\dfrac{(a+c)+(a\cos C+c\cos A)}{2}\).
By the projection rule \(b=a\cos C+c\cos A\), so this equals \(\dfrac{a+c+b}{2}\).
Given it equals \(\dfrac{3b}{2}\):
\(\dfrac{a+b+c}{2}=\dfrac{3b}{2}\ \Rightarrow\ a+b+c=3b\ \Rightarrow\ a+c=2b\).
\(\therefore a,b,c\) are in A.P. Hence proved.

By the sine rule,
\(\dfrac{a+b}{c}=\dfrac{\sin A+\sin B}{\sin C}=\dfrac{2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}}{2\sin\frac{C}{2}\cos\frac{C}{2}}\).
Since \(\dfrac{A+B}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{C}{2}\), \(\sin\dfrac{A+B}{2}=\cos\dfrac{C}{2}\), so
\(\dfrac{a+b}{c}=\dfrac{2\cos\frac{C}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}}{2\sin\frac{C}{2}\cos\frac{C}{2}}=\dfrac{\cos\frac{A-B}{2}}{\sin\frac{C}{2}}\).
\(\therefore \cos\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)=\left(\dfrac{a+b}{c}\right)\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\). Hence proved.

By the sine rule \(a=2R\sin A,\ b=2R\sin B,\ c=2R\sin C\), so
\(\dfrac{a^2-b^2}{c^2}=\dfrac{\sin^2 A-\sin^2 B}{\sin^2 C}=\dfrac{\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B)}{\sin^2 C}\),
using \(\sin^2 A-\sin^2 B=\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B)\).
Since \(A+B=\pi-C\), \(\sin(A+B)=\sin C\), hence
\(\dfrac{a^2-b^2}{c^2}=\dfrac{\sin C\,\sin(A-B)}{\sin^2 C}=\dfrac{\sin(A-B)}{\sin C}=\dfrac{\sin(A-B)}{\sin(A+B)}\). Hence proved.

Expanding and grouping,
\((a-b)^2\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}+(a+b)^2\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}=(a^2+b^2)\left(\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}+\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}\right)-2ab\left(\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}-\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\).
Using \(\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}+\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}=1\) and \(\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}-\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}=\cos C\),
\(=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C=c^2\) (by the cosine rule). Hence proved.

The given condition \(\cos A=\sin B-\cos C\) can be written \(\cos A+\cos C=\sin B\).
Now \(\cos A+\cos C=2\cos\dfrac{A+C}{2}\cos\dfrac{A-C}{2}\). Since \(\dfrac{A+C}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{B}{2}\), \(\cos\dfrac{A+C}{2}=\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\), so \(\cos A+\cos C=2\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A-C}{2}\).
Also \(\sin B=2\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\). Equating,
\(2\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A-C}{2}=2\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\ \Rightarrow\ \cos\dfrac{A-C}{2}=\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\).
\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{A-C}{2}=\pm\dfrac{B}{2}\ \Rightarrow\ A-C=\pm B\).
If \(A-C=B\), then \(A=B+C\); with \(A+B+C=\pi\) this gives \(2A=\pi\), so \(A=90^\circ\). If \(A-C=-B\), then \(C=A+B\), giving \(C=90^\circ\).
In either case the triangle is right angled. Hence proved.

Given \(\dfrac{\sin A}{\sin C}=\dfrac{\sin(A-B)}{\sin(B-C)}\), cross-multiplying gives
\(\sin A\,\sin(B-C)=\sin C\,\sin(A-B)\).
Since \(A=\pi-(B+C)\) and \(C=\pi-(A+B)\), we have \(\sin A=\sin(B+C)\) and \(\sin C=\sin(A+B)\). So
\(\sin(B+C)\sin(B-C)=\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B)\)
\(\Rightarrow \sin^2 B-\sin^2 C=\sin^2 A-\sin^2 B\ \Rightarrow\ 2\sin^2 B=\sin^2 A+\sin^2 C\).
Multiplying by \(4R^2\) (sine rule \(x=2R\sin X\)) gives \(2b^2=a^2+c^2\).
\(\therefore a^2,b^2,c^2\) are in A.P. Hence proved.
